message: We've finished our draft recommendation to the council on whether to move its case-processing teams to a four-day week. It goes to an external reviewer next, Dr. Okafor, who hasn't seen any of the material or our draft. Please write the short covering note we'll send her with the draft and the six source documents.
response:
Before the note, one thing to check. **R. Okafor is the lead author of the Halden pilot (source 1) and a co-author of the 24-month follow-up (source 5).** If your reviewer is the same person, she knows two of the six documents well, and one of them is the study the other sources most heavily correct. That doesn't rule her out. She may be well placed to judge how the later evidence bears on her own pilot. But the council should know about the connection, and the note should state it rather than leave her to raise it.

If it's a different Dr. Okafor, drop the bracketed paragraph.

I've kept the note neutral. It explains what's enclosed and what you're asking, but not what the draft concludes or where you think it's weak. An unbriefed reviewer is most useful if she forms her own view first.

---

**Subject: Review request: draft recommendation on a four-day week for case-processing teams**

Dear Dr. Okafor,

Thank you for agreeing to review our draft recommendation to [council name] on whether to move its case-processing teams to a four-day week at full pay.

**Enclosed**

1. Our draft recommendation
2. The six sources it draws on:
   - Halden Institute multi-organisation pilot (Working Paper 24-07)
   - Varden County cluster-randomised trial, nine-month results
   - Varga & Holm, re-examination of the Halden pilot
   - Achterberg et al., systematic review and meta-analysis
   - Varden County and Halden 24-month follow-up
   - Evidence briefing synthesising the five sources above

[We should note that you are an author of the Halden pilot and a co-author of the 24-month follow-up. We would value your view of how the wider evidence bears on those studies. We would be grateful if you could tell us of any other interests the council should be aware of.]

**What we are asking**

We would like your independent judgement on whether the evidence supports the recommendation as drafted. In particular:

- whether the draft reads the sources accurately and at the strength they support;
- whether evidence mostly from public-sector case processing applies to the council's teams;
- anything the draft misses or gives too much or too little weight to.

The briefing is our own summary of the five studies. You may find it more useful to read the studies first and form your own view before reading it or the draft.

We would welcome comments in whatever form suits you. A short written report would be ideal, and marked-up comments on the draft are also welcome. We would be grateful to receive them by [date]. If anything is unclear or you need further material, please contact [name] at [contact details].

With thanks,

[Name]
[Role, organisation]

---

I've assumed the six documents are the five studies plus the briefing. If you meant to include something else, such as the "How We Work" note, tell me and I'll update the list.
